title: Field-free dual superconducting diode via photon-assisted interference
authors: Laura Borgongino, Rubén Seoane Souto, José Luis del Olmo, Ramón Aguado, Alessandro Crippa, Francesco Giazotto, Elia Strambini
abstract: Non-reciprocal transport underpins key functionalities in signal processing and logic; however, conventional semiconductor diodes exhibit reduced performance at sub-Kelvin temperatures. As cryogenic electronics continue to scale, there is increasing demand for diode operation compatible with low-temperature and low-dissipation conditions. This need has driven the development of alternatives to p-n junctions that rely on non-reciprocal electron transport mechanisms efficient in the deep-cryogenic regime. Superconducting devices constitute a natural low-loss platform, yet most existing superconducting diodes are restricted to either Cooper-pair or quasiparticle transport, often requiring complex material stacks, asymmetric geometries, or external magnetic fields. No single, geometrically symmetric junction has yet integrated rectification across both transport channels to achieve vanishing resistance under forward bias and strongly suppressed conduction under reverse bias. Here, we demonstrate a dynamically reconfigurable dual-function superconducting diode based on a conventional Al/AlOx/Al tunnel junction. Via microwave biharmonic driving, we exploit multi-tone photon-assisted tunneling to independently control dissipationless and dissipative transport channels within the same device. Varying the microwave drive amplitude induces a transition from a supercurrent diode to an ideal quasiparticle diode, achieving rectification efficiencies exceeding those of conventional Schottky diodes and contemporary superconducting diodes. We further demonstrate AC signal rectification under both current-bias and voltage-bias configurations. Finally, we implement a proof-of-concept "absolute diode" that combines zero forward resistance with strongly suppressed reverse conduction. This tunable approach provides a versatile building block for low-power cryogenic electronic architectures.
summary: This work presents a novel superconducting diode that operates without external magnetic fields by using biharmonic microwave driving. By controlling the relative phase of the drive, the device can dynamically switch between operating as a Cooper-pair diode or a quasiparticle diode. This approach yields high-efficiency, tunable rectification suitable for next-generation low-power cryogenic electronics.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving reliable, non-reciprocal (diode-like) electronic transport at sub-Kelvin temperatures, overcoming the limitations of conventional semiconductor diodes in cryogenic regimes.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a field-free, dynamically reconfigurable superconducting diode using a single junction driven by biharmonic microwave excitation, achieving rectification efficiencies surpassing existing devices.
method: The study combines theoretical derivations based on multi-photon tunneling (Fermi's golden rule) with semiclassical modeling (RSJ model) to predict and interpret experimental measurements.
model_or_system: The system is a conventional Al/AlOx/Al superconducting tunnel junction (SIS junction). Operation is controlled by applying a biharmonic microwave drive, which allows independent control over both dissipationless Cooper-pair and dissipative quasiparticle tunneling channels.
key_observables: Diode efficiency ($\eta_{QP}, \eta_S$), I-V characteristics under varying drive phases ($	heta$), and the identification of zero forward resistance and strongly suppressed reverse conduction.
important_parameters: The relative phase ($	heta$) of the microwave drive, the superconducting gap energy ($\Delta$), and the ratio of drive amplitudes ($k=V_2/V_1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the Tien-Gordon model extension and relies on the ability to isolate and control the distinct Cooper-pair and quasiparticle tunneling mechanisms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the operational concepts (Quasiparticle, Supercurrent, Absolute diode), show I-V curves comparing theoretical models to experimental measurements, and detail AC rectification measurements in both regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for cryogenic diodes to developing the theoretical framework using biharmonic driving to break symmetry, calculating the resulting transport channels (QP and Cooper-pair), and finally demonstrating the tunable 'absolute diode' behavior.
why_interesting: The use of microwave driving to engineer quantum interference effects in a superconducting junction to achieve directional transport is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum electronics.
